## Natural history notes

A small songbird characterized by its olive-brown upperparts, bright yellow throat and breast, and rounded tail, with males showing a distinctive black facial mask bordered by pale gray or whitish above. In Florida, it is found in marshes, wet prairies, pond edges, mangroves, brushy wetlands, ditches, fields, and other dense low vegetation, especially near water. It feeds mainly on insects, spiders, and other small invertebrates, usually foraging low in grasses, reeds, shrubs, and tangled vegetation.
